sample_queries.question: What is the role of the Raft cluster leader during log replication?
sample_queries.answer:
Once the entry has been replicated on a majority of cluster nodes, the leader commits the entry and applies it to its local state machine before responding to the client. [Context Source 3: halueval_halueval-qa-005.txt (Chunk 0) (relevance: 0.555)]
In the Raft protocol, client requests are directed exclusively to the elected leader, which appends the command to its log as a new entry. [Context Source 4: ragtruth_ragtruth-qa-003.txt (Chunk 1) (relevance: 0.540)]
To prevent stale reads from leaders that have been partitioned from the cluster, the leader must contact a quorum of the cluster to verify its leadership before responding to read-only queries, or utilize lease-based read optimizations.
sample_queries.reference: The Raft leader receives client commands, appends them to its log, sends AppendEntries RPCs to followers in parallel, and commits the entry once safely replicated on a majority quorum of servers.
